classification.difficultyReason: Convert a bearing to an acute triangle angle and calculate an eastward distance.

content.prompt:
A bushwalker walks 4 km on a bearing of $055^\circ$ from point $A$ to point $B$.
Find how far east point $B$ is from point $A$, correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Compass rose at A, northeast segment AB, two endpoint dots and an unlabelled clockwise bearing arc. Ordinary source colours become black.
spec.mathematics: AB lies on bearing 055 degrees; endpoint direction is (sin 55 degrees, cos 55 degrees).
spec.answerVisibility: No numerical angle, distance or answer is printed in the question diagram.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the eastward distance in kilometres. The angle between $AB$ and east is $90^\circ-55^\circ=35^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\cos35^\circ&=\frac{x}{4}\\x&=4\cos35^\circ\\x&\approx3.28\text{ km}\end{align*}$$
